The explosions were terrible, earth-shaking, although this is about 15 kilometres, perhaps about 13 kilometres away as the crow flies from the church and mosque to the place where I was. I didn't know that night what this was all about, but in the morning I heard from the people who lived there, who lived in the area and who I know, they told me that the church and the mosque had been blown up. The pretext was that Muslim and Serb extremists, that's the story I heard from them, they did that. That Muslim and Croat extremists did that in order to blame the Serb side for all this. That's the story that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking quickly again at P1128.8, you said this was the Catholic church in Prijedor. Do you know when that was damaged or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same night when the mosque was, but I don't know which one happened first. Because there were two explosions at the same time. I mean, at the same time, within ten minutes' time, within ten minutes' time, there were two explosions more or less. So over a short period of time, after midnight, two explosions were heard. And now which one was the first one I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with those photographs. Your Honour, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Now, Mr. Mesanovic, as I explained to you yesterday, the lead counsel for the accused Brdjanin will be cross-examining you. And your duty is to answer his questions as fully and as truthfully as possible. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you need any help, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think I'll get there, Judge. I'm just getting close.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't have a lot of questions to ask you, and I think we can get through this rather quickly, if you will listen very carefully to the questions that I ask you and try to answer them as precisely as you can and in as short a way as you can, we'll get you out of here today and you can go home. Okay.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to talk to you first about that time in late July which you said was either late July or early August when a delegation came to the Omarska camp from Banja Luka. All right. Where were you when that delegation arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the glass house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Would you look at 1128.17 and 1128.18 and show us exactly where you were.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the time, throughout the six weeks, as I said, I was here, there's an open space in the middle between the restaurant, the entrance to the restaurant, the corridor leading to the cloak room or as we referred to it later, the big dormitory. So there's a space in between where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So that's where you were when that delegation came there?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's in the upper right, in the extreme right corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that's where you were during the entire time that delegation was there?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the six weeks except for the first three days, as I said, at the beginning that I had spent in the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How long was the delegation from Banja Luka present in the camp?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where did the delegation enter the camp?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably through the main gate to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You didn't see them come in?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where did they go after they came in?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say really. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where were they when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in this area, outside the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you were able to see through that building that's the restaurant and see them from the glass house where you were through the restaurant to the other side?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, through the glass panes of the restaurant because that's a building made of glass, both the restaurant and the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Were you wearing glasses then?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was ten years younger at that time. I've only worn glasses for the last two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This was in the heat of the summer. It was probably what, 35 degrees that day?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea really.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Hot, though?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you've described a person showing up in a dark suit?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did that person have grey hair?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to know. He was a rather short man. I can't quite remember. I had other things to worry about. I can't remember. I only said someone told me who was coming and when they were coming, and we were supposed to greet them with the three fingers, the colour of their hair, the colour of their suit or their eyes, I'm sorry, I can't remember. It has been ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So were you just guessing when you said this person was wearing a dark suit?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't guessing, but people who were nearer to him. Because I suppose he was the one who got the most attention, and what I learned from my experience is that he would then be the central personality, the most important person if he was the one being extended the greatest amount of attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you just assumed that because this one person was getting the most attention that it must have been Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, when the same question was put by the Prosecution, you objected. Your objection was sustained, and now you're doing exactly the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Judge, I agree. I'm stopping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You told us that you had seen Mr. Brdjanin on TV very frequently. Before you went to --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So I assume Mr. Brdjanin would have been a person that you would have been able to recognise.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, it is the case, isn't it, that in just a few days after that Banja Luka delegation came, Omarska was basically closed down, and everybody was moved out. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, not everyone had been moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All but about a hundred?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... left there --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: -- delegation came?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. You mean the majority? Yes. The majority yes, but the rest of them, I don't know when they were moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know who it was from that Banja Luka delegation that notified the world press that Omarska was a horrible place and they should come there? Do you remember who it was that notified them, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that anybody from that Banja Luka delegation exposed Omarska to the world?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only heard --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard about journalists having done that, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you know that just a very few days after that delegation came there, that Roy Gutman wrote an article about Omarska and exposed Omarska to the world. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the document P1263, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May I see it before you give it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor earlier today. And the Prosecutor asked you to read the first paragraph thereof which involves the dismissal of people from executive posts and posts involving a likely flow of information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That document dated 22 June, 1992, is it not?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember the dates on all the dismissal documents that the Prosecutor then showed you? Do you remember that they were 2 May and 4 May and 5 May and 7 May?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So they couldn't possibly have anything to do with that document you're looking at, could they?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with this document, not in terms of the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now I'd like you to be shown a document P1182, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: First thing, you saw this document yesterday, sir. I think you probably remember it. It's dated 4 May of 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know that there was no ARK Crisis Staff on 4 May, 1992? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The power was taken over on the 30th of April, and then came the 1st of May, Saturday, Sunday, Monday. I think Monday was the 4th of May. There was an incident on the Prijedor/Dubica Road. All Muslims who were found in the bus were killed, and then after that curfew was introduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What I'm interested in, sir, is for you to look at -- first of all, I'd like you to read the first paragraph of this document. Would you just do that, for us, read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to decision number 1/92 of 16 of April, 1992, of the ministry of national defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and due to a change of circumstances on the territory, and in order to defend and protect the nation and its assets, and to preserve the peace in these parts, the government of AP Krajina reached..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, would you go to the last page and look at where the stamp is. Can you read what the stamp says.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "TO staff, Banja Luka, socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, TO staff, Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Doesn't say anything about the Autonomous Region of Bosanski Krajina, does it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's because they didn't have a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How do you know they didn't have a stamp?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because yesterday and today, I have been shown a number of documents dated after the 30th of April with different headings, Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, Srpska Republika, Republika Srpska, so I suppose they didn't even have a stamp of their own on the 4th of May, so they used whatever they had, just like the typewriters. Some of them used Cyrillic letters and some of them used Latin lettering. Excuse me, please, Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the stamp reads the socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so they didn't have their own stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look at P1190, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before he does that, Mr. Ackerman. We look at the same document, P1182, the front page, very top, the second line is at least translated in the English version as "The Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I was only referring to the stamp, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. But I wanted to highlight that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: P1190, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Again, you were shown this yesterday, and I want to call your attention to paragraph 2 under "conclusions." First of all, this is the minutes of the meeting of the National Defence Council of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor on the 5th of May. That would be the next day after the decision we just looked at regarding mobilisation signed by Mr. Sajic. On the next day, there's a conclusion of the National Defence Council that reads as follows, does it not: "The mobilisation orders following from the decision of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina Assembly are to be carried out when the actual situation in the municipality renders it necessary and in accordance with the needs and a special plan through callup papers issued by the municipal secretariat for national defence." So the National Defence Council in Prijedor is saying "we will comply with that decision when we think it is appropriate for us to do so." Right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, if you look now, sir, at Document P1218 --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but this may be interesting for the Court. Decision of the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina, in that system, could never be carried out or implemented. Because in order for mobilisation in that system, it was clear who was in a position to issue it, but by no means an assembly of an autonomous region which had never existed up to the takeover in Prijedor. That's at least in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Look now, will you, sir, at 1218. Now, I think, sir, that this is actually the decision on 22 May, 1992, when there was a decision for mobilisation in the Prijedor Municipality. And if you look at just the first paragraph of this document --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't get the interpretation. Yes, all right. I can hear it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay, we're looking, sir, at a document dated 22 May, 1992, which appears to be the actual Crisis Staff decision for mobilisation in Prijedor Municipality. And it recites as the basis for the decision, does it not, "The decision of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina about the general public mobilisation of forces and materiel in the republic." Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And so as you have -- as you have pointed out, they couldn't have relied upon anything coming from the Autonomous Region of Krajina, but did rely on a decision from the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But it's an illegal institution. A parallel institution at that time. There was the official Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your position about that, sir, and it's not my intention to argue with you about that at all. You may take that position, and we'll all understand that that's your position. I want you to look now at -- and I want to just talk a little bit -- well, let's go a different way. Look at 1268, please. Now, a few moments ago, sir, we had looked at that document dated the 22nd of June signed by Milorad Sajic. I'd like you now to look at a conclusion of the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality, number 116. Could you find that for me, please. You have to -- can you hear me? Are you not getting translation again?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you. It's just that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... untranslated?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's untranslated, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I have 115, I have 117, I have 119, and 118.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was one of the conclusions that I was waving around this morning that I said had been translated, and I can provide it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have a copy, we can have it photocopied now and circulated. And in the meantime, you can proceed, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Have you found 116, sir?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you just read it in its entirety, starting at the beginning with "Pursuant to articles 3 and 7..."?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the English copy please be provided to the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Wait a minute, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't even have it ourselves, Mr. Interpreter. That's what I have asked for. In the meantime, not to waste time, please start reading it slowly, and the interpreters will translate it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Maybe it's better if I read it in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have it in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then you read it in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let's do this. Put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or we could put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I've got yellow highlighting on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But that's not a problem now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, you see this document from the Crisis Staff in Prijedor dated 23 June, 1992. Do you?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the first paragraph says: "The Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality does not accept and considers invalid all decisions by the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina adopted before 22 June, 1992." Number 2: "The Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality shall implement all enactments submitted to it and adopted after June 22nd, 1992, by the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region." And then number 3: "Inform the Crisis Staff about this conclusion." What they are saying there is we are not going to pay any attention to any of your pronouncements until after June 22nd, and they are informing the Autonomous Region Crisis Staff that they are ignoring their pronouncements up until that time, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: See if you can find decision number 118, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do we have a translation of that one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we do have that one translated, yes. If we could have it put on the ELMO, usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it comes out of order in the English translation, so it's at page 0086-7006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This one is dated 25 June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it says: "The Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina is hereby requested to organise a regional secretariat for national defence and make it operational as soon as possible." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, remember again that document of 4 May that we looked at signed by Milorad Sajic, which said that it was a regional secretariat for national defence. If the authorities in Prijedor were aware of such a document, isn't it curious that they would now be telling the Autonomous Region of Krajina that they should organise a regional secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what your question would be specifically. The municipal secretariat for national defence did exist before the war, republican secretariat and the federal secretariat as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But we're talking about the regional secretariat, that didn't exist, did it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no it did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you saw that document dated 4 May that purported to be a document from the regional secretariat which you've already told us would not have been possible, and then on the 25th of June, the Crisis Staff is telling the Autonomous Region of Krajina what to do, in effect. They are telling them to organise a regional secretariat for national defence. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. One more. Look at decision number 119 now. It's dated the same date. It's dated 25 June.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's just paragraph 1 that I'm interested in there, sir. And it says, does it not, that "The Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality shall not implement enactments adopted by the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina until the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina has elected all members of the government respecting the principle of equal representation of municipalities through the election of their candidates for members of the government." Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So they have said they are not going to pay any attention to the decisions of the Crisis Staff of ARK. They are now saying they are not going to pay any attention to the enactments of the government of ARK until further notice, aren't they? Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to look now at some documents from the Autonomous Region of Krajina after June 22nd. The first one I want you to look at is P260. What you have before you, sir, is a decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina dated 24 June, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So this would be a document after the 22nd of June that they said that they would implement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look at the -- the first thing I want you to look at is the signature. Do you notice that it is not signed by Mr. Brdjanin, but has a "Za" there?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The part that I'm interested in is number 2. It says that "only Cyrillic script may be used in public communication." Doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, I want you to now look at four documents that you can look at altogether rather quickly, 1271, 1272, 1273, and 1274. 1271, sir, is a ruling of the executive committee of the municipality of Prijedor, and it's June 30th, after the ARK decision saying "everything should be in Cyrillic" and it's not in Cyrillic, is it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 1272 is dated 30 June --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the stamp is an old one, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. 1272, dated 30 June, ruling by the executive committee is not in Cyrillic, is it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have any typewriters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This was obviously written on a typewriter.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they didn't have typewriters with the Cyrillic alphabet because all the typewriters went missing and we didn't have a single one in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So there were no Cyrillic typewriters in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember the Official Gazette that we have looked at several times over the last few days? I think published --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was printed at the printing press. Official Gazettes are usually printed at printing presses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But it was not in Cyrillic either, was it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read one that was written in Cyrillic. I can't remember which one exactly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Take a quick look at P1268, again, sir. If you just want to be certain about that.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 27th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Look now please at another exhibit, Your Honours, it's DB97 -- 98, DB98.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This, sir, is a decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina dated 24 June, 1992. The first thing I'll call your attention to, again, is the signature is not that of Mr. Brdjanin, but says "Za." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. But usually, drawing on my own experience, my secretary could authorise me to sign something on his behalf. So he authorised someone, some of his closest associates, to sign for him. But it only had to be a person who you authorised. It cannot be just anyone. It can be an authorised person who also had the seal. I'm talking about before. Every worker had the seal of the secretariat for national defence, but they did not have the right to sign anything, only authorised persons had the right to sign their names on documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a meeting of several municipalities called the Sanska Una association of municipalities that met, I think, in May?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And voted to try to get rid of Mr. Brdjanin and replace him with Mr. Kupresanin? Are you familiar with that at all?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I was not given access at all. I only continued doing what I could do, but this was all on their orders, orders of my colleagues from work, not the secretary any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You don't know if Mr. Brdjanin authorised anybody to sign this document for him, do you?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I said that in the practice that existed, and I think that that applies generally, I said who could sign a document. Only authorised persons, that's what I said. It can't be just anyone signing an official document, an official document of a particular institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But it would be someone to whom you would entrust the stamp and give them authority to sign, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What does the stamp say on this document?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because it says "For the president."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What does the stamp say?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Banja Luka, the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," and then it says, "Banja Luka" in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It says the "assembly," it doesn't say the Crisis Staff, does it?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. It's a technical matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know the Crisis Staff had its own stamp?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. This document says, in paragraph 2: "Immediately check military conscripts of Serbian nationality without a registered domicile and place of residence in the Autonomous Region of Krajina who failed to register with the competent secretariat for national defence. "Organise their transfer to the municipalities from which they departed and turn them over to the competent secretariat for national defence." Do you know if the authorities in Prijedor implemented that decision?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th of June, 1992. If this was in the morning, after 9.30, I was already in a cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But my question was do you know if that was implemented, because you heard things even after you were in a cell.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was that? How could I hear about it in a cell whether a decision had been implemented. I was arrested on the 24th of June, 1992, around 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So the answer is you don't know?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How about paragraph 3, do you know that one? "Check all persons wearing uniforms without authorisation and pretending to be members of military organs and organs of the interior and act in keeping with the law on law and order and other laws, disarm them and take away their uniforms and act in keeping with legal regulations." Do you know if that was implemented in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same document. Believe me, I don't know. The same document. After the meeting, minutes are typed out. Could have been on the 25th, and then antedated the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's the case, sir, that you don't know of anything that was done in Prijedor on the directions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, do you?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there re-examination, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, can you just look at the document, I think DB98. Mr. Ackerman took you to II and asked you about whether you knew whether the military conscripts of Serbian nationality who hadn't been registered and who failed to register were turned over to the competent secretariat for national defence. He asked you whether that had been implemented in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know because I had been arrested on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that document is dated the 24th of June, 1992. And he also asked you -- he put it to you that you didn't know about anything that had been carried out at the directions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina in Prijedor. I want to take you to several documents now. The first one you looked at a moment ago, which is P1182. That is the document dated the 4th of May signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Sajic.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 calls for a general public mobilisation on the entire territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. This is not a Crisis Staff document. The question has to do with the Crisis Staff. This is not a Crisis Staff document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Where are you heading, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm going to show the witness a number of documents which show that the mobilisation was implemented in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we're talking -- the document DB98 is dated 24th of June, 1992. So if there was an implementation, in a sense, of a mobilisation dated 4th May of 1992, it's preceding the decision of the -- or the order of the Crisis Staff. And therefore can never amount to an implementation of that order. So I would allow you to make reference to any document that is post-24th June, 1992, but not anteceding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I confused myself. I didn't want that document for that reason. I wanted it for another reason. And then I will go back to another document Mr. Ackerman showed the witness for the same point I was about to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, looking at DB98, Mr. Ackerman took you to the stamp of that document and said that that was the Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly. Can you please read out the block of the document on the top left-hand corner of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. I was referring to the stamp, not the block in the upper left-hand corner. The whole question had to do with where the stamp was from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there can be an explanation for that, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: His answer to me that caused that question was you can authorise someone to use your stamp and sign your name "Za," and the whole point of the question was that this was not someone who was authorised to use the stamp of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina because what they used was the stamp of the Assembly. And --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the witness has just testified that they used the stamp because there may not have been a stamp for the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff, and so the Assembly stamp was used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not argue in front of the witness. Put your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, can you please read the block on top of the document dated the 24th of June, 1992, of DB98.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I have to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But your objection is not being sustained because --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have a different objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have a different one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My objection is that before I asked him a question about this, I told him it was a document of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And all she is doing is asking him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hear --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: -- if that's what it is. Of course it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- what the question is first. And then if you are right, I will ask him not to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I can see that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hear it first. I mean, I am not going to stop Ms. Sutherland before she asks the question. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, can you please read the block on the top left-hand corner of the document.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Crisis Staff, Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff, would that be part of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly, part of the same government?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I'm confused. Let me just tell you what I've learned on the basis of my experience. This is what we called a letterhead, and it had to correspond to the stamp. So probably in their hierarchy, the Crisis Staff was probably subordinated to the Autonomous Region. The Autonomous Region could give orders to the Crisis Staff. The stamp does not correspond to this, and the two have to be the same. The letterhead and the stamp. Once it says Serb, once it says Assembly, and then there is this stamp that is used, it's quite simple.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was it your testimony earlier in response to a question by Mr. Ackerman in relation to the stamp that there may not have been a stamp for the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because they used the stamp of the socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Assembly of Banja Luka. It did not say the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whatever. So they used the old stamp, but a new letterhead like on many other documents where the two did not coincide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in other words this is a supposition, having seen other documents with this so-called anomaly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The old stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is your conclusion or your supposition or your belief that the reason for that is they did not have a proper stamp for the Crisis Staff of the ARK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, I assume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P1182.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is the decision --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- you've seen on a couple of occasions dated the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it's from the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina, regional secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the decision calls for a general public mobilisation on the entire territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That all conscripts on the territory are obliged to be at the disposal of the municipal TO headquarters. And then number 5, all paramilitary formations and individuals in possession of illegal weapons and ammunition are asked to surrender those weapons and ammunition immediately, and it continues to the municipal TO headquarters or the nearest public security station. That's at the Autonomous Region of Krajina level. Can I take you now to P1190, which are the minutes of the National Defence council of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor held on the 5th of May, 1992, the day after the previous document. Does it state there under conclusions, under number 2, that the mobilisation orders following from the decision of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina Assembly are to be carried out? Mr. Ackerman asked you questions on that, and then paragraph 7: "All paramilitary units and individuals who possess weapons and ammunition illegally are called upon to surrender them immediately. And it goes on to the public security station in Prijedor or its nearest office.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In your view, are the minutes of the 5th of -- the National Defence Council on the 5th of May implementing the decision of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina regional secretariat for National Defence of the 4th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this. It's not even possible because paragraph 2 refers to a decision of the Autonomous Region Assembly, and there is no decision of the Assembly that we've seen regarding mobilisation. It's just the secretariat for National Defence. So it can't possibly be referring to the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's your position on Mr. Ackerman's objection, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness can answer the question in relation to mobilisation in the Prijedor area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But your question was a very direct one. It's very specific. In your view, are the minutes of the 5th of May, the National Defence Council, on the 5th of May implementing the decision of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina, regional secretariat for National Defence of the 4th of May, 1992? You're obviously referring to the mobilisation in particular.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If the witness can look at conclusions -- in the document P1182, the decision paragraph numbered 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that identical or does that --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- in the conclusion of the 5th of May, 1992, at paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me make this clear: The Autonomous Region of Krajina, that's a region, that's an area that's part of the country. And the Assembly is the body representing the people living in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I understand that. If you look at paragraph 5 in the decision of the 4th of May, is that the same as the decision in the Prijedor NDC minutes in paragraph 7?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7. Correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you also look back to P1182 of the 4th of May, if you look at paragraph 4, the president's of the all people's defence councils are responsible for implementation of this decision and are given the authority to do so. In your view, with your experience of 13 years in the mobilisation department in the people's -- secretariat for people's defence, are the minutes of the 5th of May of the Prijedor National Defence Council implementing the decision of the 4th of May issued by the regional secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, the 4th of May document, P1182, specifically in the introductory part specifically says the decision is not of the regional secretariat for National Defence, but the decision is of the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. And under the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina it talks about the regional secretariat for National Defence. That's the block.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's the confusion. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P1195.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a praecipe of the minutes of the SDS municipal board meeting held on the 9th of May, 1992. The title block at the top left-hand corner is the Serbian democratic party of Bosnia-Herzegovina, SDS municipal board, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can I take you to halfway down the page where it mentioned Milan Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does it say there that instructions and decisions are being forwarded from the top, and the functions of the government at the level of Krajina can now be felt?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can I take you now to Prosecution Exhibit P194.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a decision of the Autonomous Region Krajina Crisis Staff held on the 14th of May, 1992. It's also included in Prosecution Exhibit 227, which is the entire Official Gazette of the Autonomous Region Krajina 2 of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, if you read conclusion number 1, "The Security Services Centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall consistently carry out the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina on the disarming of paramilitary units --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, we don't have this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Neither do we, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't think anybody has it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps, we could --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to Prosecution Exhibit 227.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Ms. Sutherland, we have over stepped our time limit. We need to make a break. In the meantime, please procure, if you are going to refer to other documents which were not already in the bundle that we had prepared for this witness, please make sure that they are available. In the meantime, we'll stop for -- would you agree 15 minutes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, just before the break, I asked you to look at Exhibit P194. Could you also -- do you have that exhibit, P194? And that's a decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have it yet. And I thought we were going to get copies during the break so we could all have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I thought we were going to our binders. Have you got P194? It's part of Prosecution Exhibit 227, do you have that, the Official Gazette 2 of 1992, the entire ARK Official Gazette? It's in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was it on the list for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, it's re-examination, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously it wasn't. But this is what I tried to make you understand before we had a break, that in our case, it's not a big deal because we can get our secretaries and they can bring the binders up, even though that is time consuming. But I don't expect the Defence to bring with them all the binders and all the documents that have been tendered so far in these 11 months or 10 months so that when all of a sudden, we come across one document that has not been indicated to them before, they are expected to dig it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I take your point, Your Honour. This is a document that has been referred to on a number of different occasions, P227.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we were not prepared for it, and understandably so because it's re-examination. Mr. Ackerman couldn't have been prepared for it as well, and while I can only blame myself if I don't have it here because I could get it through my secretary, I can't blame Mr. Ackerman if he hasn't got it right in front of him available.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I apologise for not having the copies for the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you have an extra copy available, perhaps we could place it on the ELMO, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The English translation is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, this is a conclusion from a meeting of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina held on the 14th of May, 1992. Can you read the first paragraph of the conclusions -- actually, I will read it for you. It states: "The Security Services Centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall consistently carry out the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina on the disarming of paramilitary units and individuals who are illegally in possession of weapons and ammunition. "The weapons should be handed over to the nearest public security stations where officers shall issue receipts confirming the return of weapons." And that is -- has a signature block of the president, Radoslav Brdjanin. Can I take you now to Prosecution Exhibit P1195 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we put the signature block that has just been referred to on the ELMO so you can see what it looks like. There is no signature and there is no stamp, and I object to this document on that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: There is a signature and there is a stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see it. Can you put it on the ELMO, usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a dispatch in the form of a fax, but it's not a scanned fax. It's a typewritten fax. I can't remember what the machine is called. Because that's the form of the letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then in the end, you have the code as to who has sent the number and whom it was sent to. The name, what the name was, and then the machine that was used to send this. That's before faxes and scanners were used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And however, Ms. Sutherland, the document that you were flagging --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is P194.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- to show that it had a stamp after Mr. Ackerman had objected indeed had or showed a stamp, but I don't see a stamp on what we have on the ELMO now. Is it the same document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This is -- as the witness correctly points out, the B/C/S version of Exhibit P194 is, in fact, a fax. The copy that I was provided this afternoon is this document which can be put on the ELMO, and it may have to be given the Exhibit Number P194.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it the same document or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's the same document, but this is the Cyrillic type with a stamp and a seal on it. So it's not the same document in form, but in substance. So I think it should be given an exhibit number, P194.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it may well be the same document in substance, but it's a different document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. I agree. Could you show that to Mr. Ackerman, please, usher, that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You see life begins to get complicated at 6.00. And it tends to get worse by the time we reach 7.00. We need someone to confirm to us that that is basically the same document as far as content is concerned, substance is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is the same document. It is not Mr. Brdjanin's signature. I think it is the signature of Boro, who was the secretary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said the signature block. I didn't say it was signed by Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The stamp is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The socialist federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which Boro was also the secretary of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Yes, all right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we mark this document P194.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the name is of Brdjanin but signed for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can this document be marked P194.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, I read out paragraph 1 of that conclusion. I would now like you to look at Prosecution Exhibit P1209.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Procedure that will be following, incidentally while the document is found, is that all these documents will then be admitted en bloc at the end, rather than each time saying this is being admitted, this is not being admitted, et cetera. If there is an objection that will be decided on the spot, but otherwise, we'll go ahead and then admit everything en bloc at the end, keeping the exhibit number that is indicated from time to time as we go along by the Prosecution and by the Defence. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, do you have a copy of P1209?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, do you have yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, we don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We have two here at the bar table.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this is P1209, minutes of the fourth meeting of the council for National Defence of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly held on the 15th of May, 1992, which is the day after the previous document we have just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have the document. I can't even -- okay, I do have it. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other copy is on the ELMO. So I suppose we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, can you go to the paragraph -- can you see where it says ad 1, ad 2 and 3, and then it says ad 4. And ad 4, the words under it say disarmament of paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, we need to move, because we are still -- what we have on the ELMO is ad 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We need to have ad 4 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Disarmament of paramilitary formations, and then a number of persons participated in the discussion, Simo Drljaca, Radmilo Zeljaja, Slavko Budimir, Rade Javoric, Milan Kovacevic, Bosko Mandic, and Ranko Travar. After the discussion the following conclusion was adopted --

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't have ad 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object to this in any event. Apparently it's being shown to you to counter my contention that Prijedor paid no attention to orders from the Autonomous Region of Krajina or its Crisis Staff, and this simply confirms that. The order in this regard from this the Autonomous Region had predetermined deadlines by such and such a date at 1500, everything like that. They are doing it their own way. They are saying we don't have any deadlines. They are doing it their own way. They don't indicate they are aware of anything coming from the Autonomous Region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's an argument, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's improper redirect, because it doesn't go to the cross-examination at all. It's brand new stuff. She is bringing in all brand new stuff here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour. I don't believe I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That happens on re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm showing that on the 14th of May a certain decision was issued by the Autonomous Region Krajina Crisis Staff. On the 15th of May the Prijedor National Defence Council have a meeting -- could I have the document so that I can show you what to put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the Elmo we have --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, to show the witness. Your Honour, the B/C/S, that page, is missing from the B/C/S version of that exhibit. I have it here. We will substitute the exhibit here. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, can you see ad 4 now in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And after the discussion I mentioned a number of names a moment ago, the following conclusion was adopted, the public security station in concert with the army command should draft the plan of disarmament after which the actual process should be set in motion [without predetermined deadlines] and with the assistance of the media.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking now at Exhibit P1268, decision number 116, which is a document that Mr. Ackerman took you to relating to the Prijedor Crisis Staff of the 23rd of June wherein it was held that they were not going to implement any of the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff before the 22nd of June, 1992. Given the documents that I have just taken you through, what is in writing and what is reality are two different things. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so it can be shown from those decisions on mobilisation and disarmament of the population issued by the ARK Crisis Staff that they were then implemented by the Prijedor Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't know what decision of the ARK Crisis Staff she is referring to. I don't think there is such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 14th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That was not a decision of the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 14th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was a decision of the government, I think, of...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 14th of May was a Crisis Staff decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Crisis Staff. What I want to know from the witness also, in addition to what you have been asking him, is if he has an explanation why in practice -- why they would have come to the conclusion number 116, what need was there and what was the reason behind that decision if, according to what the Prosecution is suggesting to you, and you seem -- you tend to agree, in practice, they were implementing the decisions of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, or of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the documents that I've seen today that were shown me, the mobilisation in certain places was ordered by the Assembly of the Autonomous Region. In some places it only says the Autonomous Region. This is practically the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality carrying out the orders of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, on your point, there is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Decision 119 that Mr. Ackerman took you to earlier that you could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I want to hear what the witness has to say about it. Because he agreed with you that there is a conflict between the practice and what was being preached.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The other matter that I wish to ask you some questions about relates to Mr. Ackerman's question to you about all the decisions issued by the executive committee of the Prijedor Municipality of the 2nd and the 4th and the 7th of May, 1992, in relation to dismissals and appointments. Dismissals of non-Serbs and appointments of Serbs to those positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He showed you a document dated the 22nd of June issued by the Autonomous Region Krajina Crisis Staff which said "only people in leading positions -- only positions can be held by Serbs." And then said to you: All these other decisions of the 2nd and the 4th and the 7th of May can't possibly relate to that decision, can they. And you answered "no." Can I take you now to Exhibit P227, which is the Autonomous Region Krajina Official Gazette number 2 of 1992. Can you look please, at conclusion number 4, which is a meeting of the Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we just wait until I can see the document before there's a question asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was simply taking the number and the date more for the usher's benefit than anybody's.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At a meeting held on the 8th of May, 1992, the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour, the documents that I was referring to were the 2nd, 3rd, 4th of May, I think. The dates are all in early May before the 8th of May. There wasn't even a Crisis Staff until the 5th. So this doesn't go to my cross-examination. It's a brand new thing, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, but it says the 4th of May, 1992, Banja Luka, in the left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me see the document because like this way, we can't work. This is the Official Gazette of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Published on the 5th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, published on the 5th, but referring to a decision of the ministry of National Defence of the Serbian --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's the first decision. Decision number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go to decision number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's a Crisis Staff decision of the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, you have to move us forward to decision number 4. I wouldn't know which page that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So now we're talking of the 8 May.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I referred to Exhibits 1174, 2 May; 1175, 2 May; 1178, 4 May; 1181, 4 May; 1188, 5 May; 1189, 5 May; 1191, 7 May --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speaker please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, slow down, Mr. Ackerman. The purpose of your question at the time was to obtain from the witness an explanation -- first a confirmation that those documents were not in Cyrillic script, but in ordinary Latin script.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Those were later documents. The purpose regarding these eight documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The decisions were not being followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There was no decision from the ARK Crisis Staff regarding dismissing people from their jobs on the 2nd, 4th, 5th, or 7th of May. And now she is going to counter that with a decision of the 8th of May. That's improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Your objection is sustained, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Besides the documents that I showed you which were dated the 2nd and the 4th and the 7th of May, 1992, were you also shown a number of documents dismissing people from their posts after the 7th of May, 1992, that I showed you earlier today?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. A woman who was replaced towards the end of her term.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: There was also a document in relation to Dr. Osman Mahmuljin which was dated after the 7th of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sutherland, you don't need to ask the witness the question because these documents were already referred to in the course of his testimony, and that can be established. The date of each document can be established. So, for example, Document P1200 is definitely dated 13th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And they all have the same preamble, Your Honour. Not one of them refers to any decision to the Autonomous Region of Krajina. They are all based upon what the Crisis Staff in Prijedor is doing totally on their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was about to take the witness to the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So go straight there, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to decision number 4, can you please read the second paragraph of paragraph number 9. I'll read it for you, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, please place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no idea where we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 8th of May, 1992. 0088 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the same document that you had in front of you a couple of minutes ago. Let's hear the question first before you object, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: There are three documents I want to take him to before there will be a question. So from paragraph 9 of the decision of the 8th of May, 1992, it states, second paragraph: "All management posts and enterprises must be held by persons absolutely loyal to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." The signature block on that document is president of the Crisis Staff, Radoslav Brdjanin. Can you now look at decision numbered 6, which is on page ERN 0088-2901. It's a meeting of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slow down, Ms. Sutherland, because the usher has to catch up with you, has got to find the two versions, in B/C/S, and the witness also. Have you found the page, the right page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Decision number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you bring the B/C/S version to me, please. And the second paragraph of the second conclusion: "Only persons loyal to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina may make decisions on the implementation of the general mobilisation in public and economic organisations." It goes on: "Decisions adopted by the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina are to be strictly respected in all public and economic organisations." Can you then, please, go to decision numbered 7, which is in the English translation 0088-2903. And that is a conclusion of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous -- I'm sorry, just going back to the conclusion on the 9th of May, the signature block is the president of the Crisis Staff Radoslav Brdjanin. Then on decision number 7: "At its session held on the 11th of May, 1992, the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina reached the following conclusion: The second paragraph under paragraph 5 reads: "Management posts in Krajina enterprises must be filled by persons who are absolutely loyal to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." And that has a signature block of the president of the executive council Nikola Erceg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not what I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm sorry, Your Honour. President of the Crisis Staff, Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, was it your experience of the people in the Prijedor municipality, were the non-Serbs of the leading posts dismissed in the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that. It can very well be that they were dismissing people in Prijedor, but the issue here is whether it was a result of anything that was being done by ARK or not. So he obviously knows people were being dismissed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he answered that question repeatedly before when he was asked to confirm all the documents that he was referred to. So I think -- I mean I think your objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So Mr. Mesanovic, this brings us to the end of your testimony in this trial. On behalf of the Tribunal, myself, and the other two Judges, I would like to thank you for having come over to give evidence. You will be given all the attention you require now after being escorted out of this courtroom to enable you to return to where you came from or where you would like to go. Once more, I thank you. And you may now leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we have got 6 minutes to decide what next. Number 1, I have been given a bundle today of statements referring to a particular witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not mentioning the name because I don't quite know whether he's a protective witness or not as yet. This is what I'm referring to. Is this a witness we are having next week?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's what I'm led to believe, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to make sure. However, in my lists --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Ms. Sutherland, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is from Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So that's not a problem. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Gustin has informed me that the statements and transcripts of the next witness, Witness 7.45, will be provided to you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the witness we were supposed to hear today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Although we need to touch base with Mr. Ackerman first. He has advised us of the redactions he wishes to make to the transcripts of that witness, and we need to speak with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make things clear, because I prefer to be precise on this. Are we referring to Witness BT3?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm sorry. Last week -- first, let me begin again. The next witness, pseudonym BT3, Witness 7.185, the Prosecution now does not intend to call her to lead certain evidence that was going to be redacted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And my legal officer spent I don't know how many hours making us a summary of what her testimony --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the decision was taken after lunch today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The reason I didn't inform you was because the witness was in the middle of testifying, and I needed to provide Mr. Ackerman with a document in relation to her not testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I haven't been able to do that yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So 7.185, you are renouncing, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We are seeking, after I speak with Mr. Ackerman, to tender the transcripts from the two trials into evidence, but we will not be calling her to testify about what has been redacted from one of those transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand she is here. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what's the next step? Who is the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next witness is the witness that you have the documentation for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
