utterances.text: All right. That's Kljuc Municipality, and not Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. How long do you anticipate your additional -- your addendum?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Korner anticipates spending at least three to four days with that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that may be in total. I think she will spend at least two days with the witness in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So she thinks that Mr. Ackerman is worth half of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because she said three days, two for her, one for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with regard to this witness, Mr. Trbojevic is going to be doing the cross-examination. He has been listening to the tapes. Mr. Brdjanin has also been listening to the tapes, but I still think there may be several hours. There's time between now and Monday for him to hear. And behind that, there is one that is just enormous in terms of the number of hours of tape. That's Witness 7.45. Somewhere here I have the number of hours. 7.45 is 36 and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What we want to know, Mr. Ackerman, and Ms. Sutherland, is once we have disposed of this Kljuc Municipality witness, who will be the first witness we'll hear for the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is 7.45, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So 7.185, we have spoken about. What's happening to 7.225 and 7.179?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I will try and be as clear possible, Your Honour. 7.225 was due to come next week -- this week. But due to commitments, he was unable to come. And he is now being placed around the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And 7.179? He was listed number 5. That's before --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was the situation where there were two extremely large witnesses back to back, and I had requested of the Prosecution to try to separate them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: To separate them, to give me a chance to be prepared. And they kindly agreed to do that. And witness number 5 agreed to come later, which moved us to then number 6, 7.45, who will be our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that I would imagine is going to take us quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is going to take quite some time, but what I would suggest to you is because of the number of hours of tape, the 36 and a half hours, and the fact that Mr. Brdjanin has to spend most of the time between now and Monday listening to the tapes of Monday's witness, that it's unlikely that we should try to start Witness 7.45 any time next week. I think we'll be four days with the major witness who is coming next week in any event, but it would be very difficult, I think, to start with that witness. We could possibly do it, but it would be difficult. The problem is, you know, not only does Mr. Brdjanin have to listen to 36 and a half hours of tape, but I have to meet with him for a significant amount of time for him to tell me what he heard on that 36 and a half hours of tape that I should know in terms of preparing my cross-examination. And frankly there isn't anybody that can help me in terms of understanding more than Mr. Brdjanin can help me, and I really rely on my conferences with him to understand this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we could start the witness on Friday, and then that would give Mr. Ackerman at least the weekend to prepare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, discuss it, please, with Ms. Korner between now and Monday when we reconvene.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can I just say, Your Honour, just in relation to the witness I said had been pushed down to the 20th of November. But we provided Mr. Ackerman with a new order of witnesses and we will give the same to the Trial Chamber this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So I understand that there is no sitting tomorrow then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. And we'll all meet, please God, on Monday. Monday next week, all the sittings are in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, unless Mr. Ackerman wishes to call this witness, 7.185, for cross-examination once he has received these documents, he may not, and he may just agree to the transcripts going in Rule 92. So perhaps if I can somehow get this document to him in the next five minutes, he can let me know whether he wants the witness to be here tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. If he will be in a position to do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm certainly willing to try. I just haven't seen the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway. These are things that can be thrashed between you. And if there is a decision along the lines that you are suggesting or hoping for, then just let us know. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All week is morning sittings next week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.33 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
